title: Compact defaults harmonizer and delta quantifier: reconcile tenant defaults with workload signals
author: Ava Robertson
description: Motivation: Tenant defaults, workload-derived defaults (sampled batch shapes, cache-presets) and operator overrides have diverged across deployments. This leads to suboptimal unit economics and surprising regressions when autoscaling or quantization rollouts happen. This PR introduces a lightweight Compact Defaults Harmonizer service plus a nightly job (delta quantifier) that reconciles, scores, and suggests safe candidate updates. What this PR does (high level): Adds a harmonizer CLI/service that ingests: (a) tenant defaults (policy-as-code store), (b) recent workload signals (heatmaps and batch shape histograms), and (c) quantization compatibility metadata. It produces: (1) reconciled defaults for batching/cache/quant profiles, (2) a delta report with risk scores and suggested rollout policies, and (3) telemetry hooks for post-rollout unit economics. The reconciler is conservative by default and emits suggested changes as a dry-run artifact stored in S3 for review. Design highlights: single-pass rules engine that prefers "no-harm" transforms: prefer smaller batch/caching deltas when latency 95th exceeds SLO; only recommend quant tier changes when compatibility score >= 0.9; annotate suggestions with per-tenant expected unit-cost delta and expected p95 latency delta. The reconciler includes a deterministic merge strategy so tenant overrides are preserved unless flagged by an explicit override rule. Files changed (high level): cmd/harmonizer/main.go - CLI entrypoint and nightly runner; pkg/harmonizer/engine.go - merge heuristics and safety gates; pkg/quant/reconciler.go - compatibility scoring and delta quantifier; internal/telemetry/harmonizer_metrics.go - new metrics and events; docs/ops/harmonizer-runbook.md - operator guidance and rollback steps; tests/harmonizer_end2end_test.go - integration test with synthetic heatmaps; charts/harmonizer/values.yaml - helm defaults. Checklist: Implement CLI + lightweight daemon mode; Merge strategy with conflict annotations; Quant compatibility scoring and conservative thresholding; Dry-run report generation + upload to S3; Unit + integration tests (synthetic workload); Telemetry: suggested_delta, risk_score, reconcile_duration; Ops docs and rollout runbook with manual approval step. Testing and CI: Added unit tests for merge heuristics and quant scoring and an end-to-end integration test that runs the CLI against a synthetic workload generator. On CI we observed one flaky test (TestHeatmapNormalization) which was stabilized by removing reliance on exact timestamp ordering; rerun green. Performance: reconciler runtime for a 2k-tenant batch is ~18s wall clock in profiling with current code path; still amenable to batching and parallel workers in a follow-up. Migration and rollout: Deploy as a nonblocking service behind feature flag reconciler.enabled=false. Nightly run emits dry-run reports to s3://redwood-prefill-dryruns/<date>/tenant-<id>.json. After 7 days of monitoring and manual approvals, we will add a canary autoapply path with tenant whitelisting. Backward-compatibility and safety: Defaults are never autoapplied without an explicit opt-in. The harmonizer emits a risk_score and predicted deltas; operator UI (separate PR) will present those. We log a full audit trail linking suggestion -> source signals -> applied changes. Related: ENG-1923 (defaults reconciliation), ENG-2050 (quant-profile compatibility matrix). Notes for reviewers: Focus on the merge heuristics in pkg/harmonizer/engine.go and the compatibility scoring in pkg/quant/reconciler.go. I kept the heuristics intentionally small to make the review tractable. If we accept larger parallelism, I'll split reconciler loop into worker pools in follow-up.

review_comments: Diego Morales: The merge strategy looks reasonable. A few nits: prefer explicit nil checks in engine.go to avoid accidental fallthroughs. Also add a small benchmark for a 10k-tenant dry run.
Ava Robertson (author): Thanks Diego - added nil checks and a micro-benchmark under tests/benchmarks. Kept it small (10k tenants runs ~85s locally); flagged for future parallelization.
Priya Shah: Quant compatibility threshold 0.9 seems arbitrary. Can you explain how you picked it and add a feature flag for tuning?
Ava Robertson (author): Threshold chosen after sampling compatibility matrices on 150 models; added reconciler.quant_threshold with a default 0.9 and documented the rationale in the runbook.
Marco Ruiz: Integration test is flaky on my machine due to time-based assertions. Can we use deterministic seeds?
Ava Robertson (author): Switched to deterministic RNG and removed wall-clock tight assertions. CI green on next run.
notes_for_ops: Deploy with reconciler.enabled=false. Run nightly job via cronjob/harmonizer-nightly with --dry-run initially. Review s3 dry-run artifacts and use redwoodctl harmonizer apply --tenant <id> --candidate <sha> to apply after manual approval.
release_notes: Compact Defaults Harmonizer: reconciles tenant defaults with recent workload signals and quant compatibility. Emits dry-run delta reports. No automatic changes applied until opt-in.
